skill.name: git-commit-message
skill.description: Generates conventional-commit messages from staged changes: type prefix + English imperative subject (≤50 chars) + optional body explaining why. Use when the user asks to write, generate, or polish a git commit message.
skill.summary: Draft Conventional Commit messages from staged changes, with concise subjects and optional bodies explaining the reason.
skill.author: alapha888

security_audit.summary: All 17 static findings are false positives: Markdown formatting, task-related Git commands, and explanatory commit text do not establish malicious execution or reconnaissance. content.value_statement: Vague commit messages make change history difficult to understand. This skill uses staged changes to draft typed subjects and optional bodies explaining the reason.
actual_capabilities: Inspect staged changes with Git diff and check staging status before drafting.
Select one of six commit types: feat, fix, docs, refactor, test, or chore.
Draft English imperative subjects with a stated limit of 50 characters.
Write optional bodies explaining the reason for changes and bug-trigger conditions.
Ask users to split changes that mix commit types.
Provide a ready-to-run Git commit command with message arguments.
limitations: Requires access to a Git repository and staged changes; an empty staging area stops message generation.
Specifies English subjects and six commit types, not a complete repository-specific convention.
Provides instructions rather than automated checks; generated subjects may need length and accuracy review.
Does not prescribe shell-escaping safeguards or guarantee safe execution of generated commands.

use_cases.title: Summarize a Bug Fix
use_cases.description: Turn a staged fix into a concise subject and a body describing the conditions that triggered the bug.

use_cases.title: Record Documentation Changes
use_cases.description: Generate a docs message that identifies the updated guidance without adding unsupported implementation claims.

use_cases.title: Review Mixed Changes
use_cases.description: Identify staged changes that combine commit types and request separate commits before drafting messages.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a First Message
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a commit message from my staged changes. Check staging first and provide the suggested Git commit command without executing it.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: prepare a message for staged work.

prompt_templates.title: Explain a Bug Fix
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect my staged bug fix. Write a fix subject and a short body stating the trigger conditions supported by the diff.

prompt_templates.title: Resolve Mixed Commit Types
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my staged changes for mixed commit types. Ask me to split unrelated changes before producing a final commit command.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Reviewed Command
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect staged changes and draft one typed subject under 50 characters. Explain why in the body and safely quote shell arguments. Do not execute.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: review command safety and message accuracy.

output_examples.input: Staged changes preserve order-list filters when moving between pages.
output: Subject: fix: keep order-list filters across pagination
Body: Preserve selected filters when users move between pages.

output_examples.input: Staged documentation changes clarify the local setup steps.
output: Subject: docs: clarify local setup steps
Body: Explain required setup steps before starting development.

best_practices: Stage only the changes intended for the commit before requesting a message.
Check that the subject and body describe evidence from the actual diff.
Review generated commands and shell quoting before execution.
anti_patterns: Requesting a message when no changes are staged.
Using chore for every feature or bug fix.
Combining unrelated changes under one vague subject.

faq.question: Which AI tools are supported?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Repository inspection requires a tool environment with Git access.

faq.question: What happens when no changes are staged?
faq.answer: The skill instructs the assistant to stop and ask the user rather than invent a message.

faq.question: Which commit types can it select?
faq.answer: It specifies feat, fix, docs, refactor, test, and chore.

faq.question: Does it create the commit automatically?
faq.answer: It instructs the assistant to output a ready-to-run command, not to execute the commit.

faq.question: Are message length and formatting enforced?
faq.answer: The instructions specify an English imperative subject of at most 50 characters. No automated validator is included.

faq.question: What should I review before running the command?
faq.answer: Check staged changes, message accuracy, subject length, and shell quoting. Generated command text still requires review.
